title: Steering issue caused tanker to crash into cruise boat, U.S. officials say
summary: The asphalt tanker vessel that struck a docked paddlewheel cruise boat in the Mississippi River at ‌New Orleans on Friday experienced a steering problem in which its rudder was stuck in one position,…

image.caption: First responders work at the scene on Friday by the riverboat American Heritage after it capsized following a collision with the tanker Atlantic Asphalt on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans. (Michael DeMocker/Getty Images)

blocks.text: The asphalt tanker vessel that struck a docked paddlewheel cruise boat in the Mississippi River at ‌New Orleans on Friday experienced a steering problem in which its rudder was stuck in one position, U.S. transportation safety officials ​said on Sunday.
National Transportation Safety Board says cause of problem not yet known
The American Cruise Lines ​passenger vessel American Heritage, with 190 people aboard, capsized at the dock, but no ​one was killed in the collision.

The ⁠Atlantic Asphalt ⁠tanker was headed ‌upriver when it experienced a "steering casualty" in which its rudder stayed in a starboard position and the vessel veered toward the river's east ⁠bank, U.S. National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) senior marine accident investigator Bart Barnum told a news conference in New Orleans.
NTSB ‌officials said they do not know what caused the steering problem. The tanker's voyage data recorder was recovered on Saturday.

Issues under investigation include ​whether the tanker's anchors were deployed and, if so, at ⁠what depth, as well as interviews with crew members ⁠and passengers, officials said. Interviews with the crew ⁠of ⁠the Atlantic Asphalt ​are scheduled over the next week, they said.
Harbour personnel, ​firefighters and ⁠onlookers scrambled to pull passengers from the cruise vessel to safety after the collision. The cruise vessel toppled over into the river.
